blurb: Long-wave physics, sources, propagation, run-up, detection, warning and risk reduction for tsunamis.

pics.alt: NOAA model map of maximum tsunami amplitude across the Pacific Ocean after the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake
pics.caption: NOAA model of the maximum open-ocean amplitude of the 11 March 2011 Tōhoku tsunami, in centimetres; black triangles mark DART stations. Energy is beamed south-eastward, perpendicular to the rupture, and steered along ridges and seamount chains.
pics.title: 2011Sendai-NOAA-Energy plot20110311.png

pics.alt: Diagram of the DART II tsunami detection system with seafloor tsunameter, surface buoy and satellite link
pics.caption: The DART II system: a seafloor bottom-pressure recorder (tsunameter) at 1,000–6,000 m depth sends data by acoustic telemetry to a moored surface buoy, which relays them by Iridium satellite to tsunami warning centres.
pics.title: DART II System Diagram.jpg
